W14-LOCAL-HASH-EXPERIMENT.md.text:
# W14 scoped local-ID lookup hashing

Production baseline is W11/6bbdcc1; HEAD702075a adds documentation only. The
3x-5x objective remains unmet. This is one isolated prototype, not a blanket
dependency upgrade or a change to RcLocal identity/hash semantics.

Native64 FxHasher1.1 hashes one u64 as id*K modulo2^64. Per-function local-ID
bases differ by2^40, so equal low40 ID bits share the same low40 initial-bucket
bits. Full hashes differ; fingerprint filtering does not eliminate probe-group
scans. The standalone pinned-Fx/std-map probe confirms this synthetic mechanism,
including controls where consecutive IDs already perform well. These operation
counts and sampled endpoint observations are not decompiler speed predictions.
Wasm32 folds two words and has a different, narrower clustering pattern.

Prototype scope: a private well-mixed hasher only for audited numeric-local maps
and membership sets whose iteration order cannot affect rewrite choice, budgets,
names, diagnostics or scheduling. Global RcLocal::Hash, local-ID creation/order,
pointer-keyed maps, externally observable interfaces and ordered worklists stay
unchanged. Avoid retaining new owners. Use explicit native-word32 finalization;
never rotate a zero-extended32-bit hash as though it were a full64-bit word.

Before ordinary timing: review all collection consumers, freeze exact UTF8/EOL
source, focused hash/lookup/usage/numeric/capture tests plus workspace/all-target
compile. Build a fresh ordinary default-feature native release with pinned
compiler/profile/allocator and explicit local-package clean/fresh=false checks.
All3978 accepted CLI sources must match. Any output change is a failed
order-independence assumption to fix or exclude, not a waived quality gate.

Ordinary comparison: W11 versus candidate, unchanged benchmark_multi.py and
manifest, unique1/unique16/small1/large1/UI1, four balanced independent process pairs,
prewarm separate, same CPU affinity, uncompressed archived binaries, all other
owned compute jobs stopped. Retain all first calls and raw outliers. Repeated
means, paired directions, medians and process peak working set are separate.
Do not multiply this ratio with earlier cohorts or infer CPU percentages from
the W13 endpoint sampler.

At least5% mean improvement in a distinct-input group with consistent paired
direction and no material regression elsewhere is the strong-success signal.
Smaller/mixed results require explicit cost/complexity review; synthetic probe
improvements alone cannot justify promotion or a whole-engine speed claim.
Do not sweep variants/rerun cohorts solely to pass a threshold.

Only a candidate worth retaining proceeds to full workspace tests, native15,
metadata/cache and actual Wasm quality. Because32-bit hashing differs, measure
matched Worker performance before claiming or promoting a Worker speed change;
an unhelpful platform-specific finalizer can retain the original hash behavior.
Validated work is committed before starting another optimization.

Pre-timing refinement: include the existing small1 corpus group to check the
extra hash arithmetic on inputs with little cross-function clustering. This is
declared before candidate screening or any W14 ordinary timing, prompted by the
synthetic consecutive-ID control, not selected after observing engine results.

wave14-hash-probe.md.text:
# W14 strided-local hash investigation

The hypothesis is real but scoped: native64 FxHasher1.1 maps equal-ordinal locals from different function ranges to the same initial bucket for every practical table mask. This is **bucket concentration, not equal full hashes**. A private lookup-table finalizer is worth an ordinary corpus experiment; synthetic probe reductions do not imply a whole-decompiler gain, much less3x.

## Exact implementation and proof

Cargo.lock pins rustc-hash1.1.0. RcLocal::hash (`ast/src/local.rs:303`) hashes only stable_id as oneu64. Fx1 starts at0; on64-bit `write_u64` does one `(state.rotate_left(5) ^ id) * K`, K=`0x517cc1b727220a95`; finish returns state without final mixing. Hence H(id)=id*K modulo2^64. Since K is odd, distinctu64 IDs have distinct full hashes.

The lifter sets id_base + function_index*(1<<40) (`luau-lifter/src/lib.rs:527,555`). For fixed ordinal, H(base+ordinal+f*2^40) differs by multiples of2^40. Its low40 bits are identical. Pinned libstd vendor hashbrown0.17.1 `raw.rs:60,82,2008` uses the low usize bits masked to table capacity for initial probing, then triangular16-bucket groups on native SSE2. Tags are a separate top7-bit fingerprint (`control/tag.rs:35`). Varying fingerprints reduce expensive key equality checks but cannot skip scanning full groups along a shared initial probe sequence.

No earlier explicit bucket-clustering analysis was found in the bounded prior-plan/summary search. Previous representation notes warned against indexing vectors by1<<40-strided IDs; that is a different issue.

## Tiny actual-map probe, no timings

External source/executable/data: `C:/Users/ADMIN/.codex/tmp/medal-ultra-wave14-hash-probe`. Compiled only a tiny standalone Rust source with pinned nightly2026-06-15 and the existing release rustc-hash1.1 rlib selected from the W13 compiler-artifact record. No Cargo/decompiler build, dependency upgrade or source edit.24 cases, at most2048 keys each; IDs are synthetic `0x123456+(function<<40)+ordinal`.

The actual std HashMap is pre-reserved; a key Eq counter records insertion/present/missing lookup comparisons. A separate Python no-delete/no-resize triangular Group16 model uses the exact actual hasher outputs; all24 cases' Eq counts agree exactly with the real maps. Group-visit counts below come from that validated **model**, not an instrumented production table.

| Synthetic keys | Finish | Mean hit groups | Mean missing groups | Actual Eq insert/hit/miss |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
|1024 functions×1ordinal|Fx1|32.5|65|3626/4650/8156|
|same|rotate_left24|1|1|2440/1024/7560|
|same|rotate_left32|4.5|9|65024/66048/131072|
|same|avalanche64|1|1.002|33/1027/56|
|256functions×8ordinals|Fx1|9.559|20|1753/3801/4822|
|same|avalanche64|1.002|1.007|58/2057/117|
|1function×2048ordinals|Fx1|1|1|0/2048/124|
|same|avalanche64|1.0005|1.0015|55/2055/124|

Rotation is not a robust fix. Rotating left24 moves variable high function bits into bucket bits, but same-ordinal tags collapse from128 to1. Rotate32 also leaves eight constant low bits and can cause far more Eq calls. Consecutive ordinals already distribute well under old Fx1, so a finalizer can add work/collisions for ordinary small single-function tables. Mixed iteration order differs; this is not globally order-neutral.

Probe mode3 native64 finalizer, applied to FxHasher::finish(), with no additive seed:

```rust
h ^= h >> 30;
h = h.wrapping_mul(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9);
h ^= h >> 27;
h = h.wrapping_mul(0x94d049bb133111eb);
h ^= h >> 31;
```

Native32 needs its own reasoning. Fx1 consumes u64 as low32 then high32 using K32=`0x9e3779b9`: `h = (((low*K32).rotate_left(5)) ^ high)*K32`. For function stride1<<40, only the low8 final-hash bits necessarily remain constant. Thus tables of at most256 buckets still share the same start for equal ordinal; larger tables partially distribute. Hashbrown32 fingerprints use bits25..31, not57..63.

Recommended explicit wrapping-u32 finalizer (return asu64 afterward):

```rust
h ^= h >> 16;
h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85ebca6b);
h ^= h >> 13;
h = h.wrapping_mul(0xc2b2ae35);
h ^= h >> 16;
```

Arithmetic-only32 check:1024same-ordinal IDs retain1024distinct full32 hashes and128tags; distinct initial heads for masks64/256/1024/4096 improve1/1/4/16→64/252/636/908. Small1function×32ordinals at64buckets goes32→23distinct heads, reinforcing the non-universal benefit. Vectors:0→0,1→514e28b7,123456→6e9c81dc,9e3779b9→92ca2f0e,ffffffff→81f16f39 (hex). No32-bit/Wasm binary was built; actual Wasm quality/performance remains required if native pilot earns retention.

## Existing W11 endpoint caller shortlist

The1306 map/set/hash self-leaf endpoint family is not entirely exposed to strided local IDs. The existing capture was re-grouped only; no new profile was run.

1. `inline_temps::collect_usage_in_statement` read/write callbacks87+34, closure capture traversal7: source uses FxHashMap<RcLocal,Usage> and recursively visits nested function bodies (`inline_temps.rs:711–751`). This is a concrete cross-function candidate. `collect_motion_facts` itself3 map leaves builds/consumes this usage table and membership sets. Its public(crate) map return/signatures and iterating consumers require explicit order/owner review before a hasher change.
2. `SubtreeUsage::record`14 map leaves: source is private FxHashMap<u64,Occurrences> keyed by stable_id (`inline_temps/usage.rs:119–148`), collects nested bodies, and query/remove uses keys. This is a smaller, better-contained lookup pilot. Its `values_mut()` finalizes independent occurrence records; preserve every order-sensitive operation inside each record. `SubtreeUsage::block`11 is the separate **pointer-key** scopes map; do not apply the strided-ID explanation to it.
3. `normalize_conditions::writes::WriteIndex`:6 block-near and2 callback-near map leaves; source has private stable-ID locals plus pointer-key scopes/seen. A private locals-only change is contained; endpoint counts cannot isolate which table contributed each folded frame.
4. Large SSA callers include write_local94,inline callback71,liveness62. These mostly operate within one function/range; the synthetic same-ordinal cross-function pattern cannot be assumed. Root's actual key-distribution census can decide exposure. Reserved-name insertion66 hashes strings. name_locals pointer identity maps and refine_names BTreeMaps are different domains.

**ICF/symbol caveat:** optimized generic symbols have aliases: SubtreeUsage::record appears under a HashMap<usize,ForOrigin> rehash symbol although source usesu64,Occurrences; collect_usage symbols show a BTreeSet payload although source usesUsage. Use source callsites to establish key domain, not the generic spelling in a sampled symbol. Endpoint counts are observations, not CPU percentages; parent/child inclusive rows must not be summed.

## Pilot boundary and acceptance

Keep Eq, Ord, stable IDs, RcLocal::hash, pointer keys, global hash aliases and dependencies unchanged. Use the finalizer only in reviewed private membership/count/lookup tables whose map iteration cannot select transformation order or names. Preserve any per-value sorting/scope order and all owner lifetimes. Corpus source hashes, diagnostics/provenance modes and actual native/Wasm behavior are the quality contract. A deterministic new order is still a potentially different output order.

Real corpora may have few repeated ordinals in the same live table, and hashing every lookup adds arithmetic even when old Fx distributes perfectly. The ordinary corpus benchmark must decide whether this saves enough work. Neither the32.5→1 synthetic group model nor1306 endpoint family supports a promised3x engine gain.

Artifacts: `wave14-hash-probe.json` (actual native counters + model), `wave14-hash-word32.json` (arithmetic-only32), `wave14-map-leaf-callers.json` (existing profile join), `wave14-hash-probe-artifacts.json` (source/rlib/binary/vendor pins). Reproduction scripts and raw JSONL remain in the C probe directory.

data.contract: Synthetic operation counts, not timings or engine-gain claims. Actual pinned rustc-hash1.1/std HashMap native64 Eq counters; separate no-resize/no-delete Group16 triangular-probe model validates exactly against those Eq counts.
Arithmetic-only exact wrapping-u32 Fx1+fmix32 model. No32-bit/Wasm binary built and no timing claims. Hashbrown32 fingerprints usebits25..31 of returnedhash.
data.recipe: h ^= h >> 16; h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85ebca6b); h ^= h >> 13; h = h.wrapping_mul(0xc2b2ae35); h ^= h >> 16;

data.contract: Existing W11 endpoint map/set/hash leaves, not CPU time

data.public_api: unchanged; private AST lookup aliases only; global RcLocal Hash unchanged

data.limits: No full suite, corpus output, release timing or Wasm runtime validation yet;32-bit tests validate arithmetic on native64 host.

data.scope: Independent read-only consumer/order/refcount audit. No source edits or builds by reviewer.

findings.evidence: ast/src/local.rs and name_locals.rs are byte-identical. RcLocal Eq/Ord/Hash and minting remain unchanged. No CFG map adaptations.
findings.conclusion: Hash finalization is confined to crate-private LocalMap/LocalSet/IdMap/IdSet aliases.

findings.evidence: inline_temps/usage.rs locals values_mut only runs Occurrences::finish independently for each key; it sorts/coalesces that key's numeric scope occurrences. scopes retains legacy FxHashMap<usize,Scope>.
findings.conclusion: Per-key finalization order cannot alter rewrite selection, local owners, or IDs.

findings.evidence: normalize_conditions/writes.rs changed only u64 locals/direct maps and required UsageMap oracle type. Indexed positions remain source ordered; admission limits use numeric counts and distinct len; pointer scopes/seen retain Fx.
findings.conclusion: Lookup/count decisions and fallback/budget behavior unchanged.

findings.evidence: Collector retains same source traversal, duplicate entry events, clone/move counts and subtree recursion. Uses are keyed queries, capture/single-write set projections, or per-local summation. copy_cleanup local_usage iteration builds independent count/site entries; pending and site BTreeSets preserve source-index ordering.
findings.conclusion: No map iteration chooses a first match, rewrite order, budget expenditure or name. Changed bucket layout can alter projection/drop order, but no owner-sensitive decision runs during those projections and final owner quantities match.

findings.evidence: Captured, stable-captured and numeric sets are consumed only by contains/membership queries. Rebuild traversal, source statement order and movement checks unchanged. Other captured projections kept as Fx still serve only membership.
findings.conclusion: No new AST owners or skipped proofs.

findings.evidence: Only references/captured u64 sets changed; visited pointer set stays Fx. The source traversal and spend calls are unchanged; stable/uncaptured methods only ask contains.
findings.conclusion: Capture scope, recursion guard and work fuel do not depend on changed iteration.

findings.evidence: waiting is inserted in source-candidate order and removed by key; each dependent Vec preserves duplicate occurrences and order. pending remains BTreeSet<(round,index)> and the16-round cap is unchanged; numbers is membership-only.
findings.conclusion: Neither candidate discovery nor propagation schedule changes.

findings.evidence: write/write_u64 delegate to the pinned FxHasher, finish applies pure native-word finalizer. Current alias keys are RcLocal/u64 only; no pointer/string/tuple map migration. Global RcLocal hash still writes exactly its stable u64.
findings.conclusion: Equality/key-first-insertion/ownership unchanged; new finalizer only changes private bucket placement.

risks_and_limits: The private aliases must never be reused later for order-sensitive iteration without a fresh consumer audit.
Different private set iteration/drop order is intentional. Current consumers are commutative or membership-only; accepted corpus/metadata/runtime/Wasm gates remain necessary.
The32-bit finalizer has code/test-model coverage in the prototype; this review does not assert an actual Wasm build/runtime passed.
No timing or speedup claim follows from this source review. Hash mixing adds arithmetic even where collision exposure is low; ordinary matched measurement decides whether to keep it.
AST sole compile coordinator reports131 focused tests and final all-target workspace check passed; all12 reviewed source hashes remain unchanged. Reviewer ran no Cargo jobs.

cpu_affinity.reason: Hybrid CPU and observed unrelated background load. Pin single-thread API samples to the same performance core; retain normal priority. Multi-thread samples use all logical processors. User processes are not modified.

data.contract: Rotated independent-process variant order; workload order reverses on alternate process rounds. First calls excluded from mean/median summaries, retained in raw rows. All accepted baseline output hashes enforced on every result. Unique removes byte-identical payload duplicates before API, so its speedup cannot be due to batch duplicate sharing. No input/filesystem cold-cache claim. Process peak working set includes loading, verification and retained results; not heap payload. Optional prewarm runs are archived separately and were declared before the cohort. Instrumented timing is diagnostic only and must not be used as performance evidence.

data.note: Ordinary native API only. All observations retained; first calls/prewarm excluded from repeat means. Peak working set is process memory, not live AST. Do not multiply with other cohorts.

data.scope: Only the exact W14 private local-ID lookup-hasher prototype, not all hash/IR designs. Main remains W11.

source_screen.verification: Existing full CLI screen record pinned; corpus was not rerun or rehashed by this timing audit.

data.reason: No >=5% distinct-input improvement, unique1 mean essentially unchanged/slower, small mean slower,16-thread direction mixed with median ratio below1; RSSdistinct essentially unchanged. No sufficient smaller-result exception.
data.cause_not_established: The ordinary cohort does not isolate why the synthetic probe-group benefit failed to transfer. Do not infer all hashing or IR redesigns are unhelpful.
